objective: V4.1 Codex-Owned Architecture, Security, and MCP Readiness - decompose Crowley's main script, lock local-first security, and create a transport-neutral tool contract for future MCP without changing existing behavior.
context: Crowley V4.0 Cognitive Memory is shipped. crowley.py has grown past 10k lines and now acts as several subsystems in one file. V4.1 is Codex-owned because the work needs sustained architectural context. Existing APIs, CLI commands, sync payloads, Actions tools, and DB schema must remain stable. ChatGPT Actions remain the compatibility contract for external tool access.
decisions: Codex owns implementation, QA, and final lock for this update.
crowley.py remains import-compatible as a facade while behavior moves into modules.
Security hardening is local-first: no OAuth, no accounts, no public full API.
MCP is prepared through a shared tool contract, but no MCP server ships in V4.1.
No schema migrations unless separately justified.
non_goals: Add OAuth, user accounts, or public full-API hosting
Require auth for localhost UI/internal routes
Build voice/TTS, automation, devices, or truth arbitration
Change public API shapes, CLI commands, sync payloads, Actions tool names, or DB schema
risks: Circular dependencies hidden by crowley.py imports
Actions catalog drift while introducing a shared tool contract
Tests becoming too broad for each slice unless focused gates are preserved
Starting V4.1 from a dirty V4 audit-fix baseline
qa_expectations: Per ticket: git diff --check, py_compile for touched modules, and focused tests for moved subsystem. Final: full unittest discovery, preflight, API smoke, Actions catalog/read/write smoke, and MCP-readiness doc audit.
next_action: Mint these tickets, then Codex starts V4.1 T0 by committing or otherwise closing the V4 audit fix and writing the deferral ledger.

approval.note: Approved in Codex thread after deciding Codex, not Cursor, owns the V4.1 architecture update.

tickets.title: V4.1 T3: MCP-ready transport-neutral tool contract
tickets.description: Introduce a transport-neutral Crowley tool contract module, likely crowley_tools.py, without changing Actions behavior. The contract must represent tool name, kind/read-write classification, description, args_schema, handler, timeout metadata, workflow tier, permission tier or write policy, and MCP candidate classification. Add mapping helpers that can produce the existing Actions catalog shape. Non-goals: do not add an MCP server; do not remove Actions registry behavior; do not rename tools.
